hero.tagline: Beneath a sky of swirling dreams & ancient verse

today.heading: Every wave returns to the sea from which it came.

moon.label: I. The Moon
moon.heading: Selene's silver chariot
moon.intro: Selene, the Greek Titaness of the Moon, drove her silver chariot across the night sky, illuminating the world with borrowed light — a reminder that even reflection can be a form of brilliance.

philosophy.label: II. The Waves
philosophy.heading: Ego, arrogance & the ocean of self
philosophy.intro: The Shiv Purana describes ego (ahamkara) as the first veil that separates the individual soul from Shiva — pure consciousness. To remove the ego is not to destroy the self but to discover its infinite nature.

gita.label: III. The Battlefield
gita.heading: Wisdom from the Bhagavad Gita
gita.intro: The Bhagavad Gita begins not with wisdom but with despair. Arjuna, the greatest warrior, drops his bow and says, 'I will not fight.' The scripture teaches that the darkest moment precedes the greatest clarity.

shiva.label: IV. The Dance
shiva.heading: Shiva & the cosmic rhythm
shiva.intro: The Shiv Purana teaches that the universe is Shiva's dance — the Tandava. Every atom moves in rhythm. Destruction is not the opposite of creation; it is its partner in an eternal dance.

art.label: V. The Canvas
art.heading: Art, beauty & the act of seeing
art.intro: Waves are the ocean's way of communicating with the shore. Each one is unique, yet all are the same water. Identity is like a wave — real in its moment, eternal in its substance.
